summary.headline: Balaji Telefilms FY26 revenue fell to INR210 crore from INR453 crore, with Q4 EBITDA loss of about INR17 crore; management guides to a FY27 top line near INR800 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR47 crore, with an EBITDA loss of about INR17 crore and loss after tax of INR14 crore, which management attributed to timing delays in content monetization and softer TV contribution. For FY26, revenue was INR210 crore against INR453 crore in FY25, with EBITDA loss of INR65.8 crore and loss after tax of INR49.6 crore. Management said the TV segment turned to a business EBITDA profit of INR4 crore in Q4 from a loss of INR7 crore in Q3. The company guided FY27 as a year of execution, with a Netflix order book of about INR350 crore and a targeted FY27 top line of around INR800 crore led by motion pictures.

financial_highlights.change: from loss of INR7 crore in prior quarter

segments.name: Television
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 business EBITDA turned to INR4 crore profit from a INR7 crore loss in the prior quarter; management says yields are still 25-30% below pre-COVID levels and shows now run 6-9 months. FY26 TV-plus-OTT-plus-B2B commissioned business was about INR160 crore, guided to about INR330 crore in FY27 (combined with B2B).

segments.name: Motion Pictures
segments.commentary: Almost no releases in FY26 (about INR15 crore revenue). FY27 guided to close to INR400 crore from four to five releases; Bhooth Bangla released with cost recovered and 3 of 4 FY27 films presold with 99% cost recovery stated.

segments.name: Digital / OTT and B2C
segments.commentary: Netflix order book of about INR350 crore, with about INR135 crore expected in FY27 and about INR50 crore added each quarter. Balaji Studios revenue guided to about INR70 crore (from INR8.5 crore), Meta to about INR115 crore (from INR6.5 crore), Hoonur talent agency to at least INR12 crore, and AstroGuide wallet recharges to INR6.5-7 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top line expected near INR800 crore: about INR300 crore from TV plus commission model, about INR400 crore from motion pictures, and about INR100 crore from B2C digital.
Digital business expected to turn cash positive in FY27; monthly cash burn was about INR50 lakh last year and is trending down.
Management expects Balaji to be a zero-tax payer for the next 4-5 years due to brought-forward losses.
Management said Q1 FY27 results will show the benefit of Bhooth Bangla returns and the turnaround, and that upside will be visible from Q1 FY27.
Expected investment of INR125-150 crore at any point in time in motion pictures; digital working capital need of INR10-15 crore.
Management said OTT margins are structurally lower than TV margins because series are finite and shot on schedule.
capex_capacity: Motion pictures: 17-movie pipeline over the next 3 years, with 4-6 movies released per year; FY27 has 4 releases, 3 presold with 99% cost recovered (management wording).
Film financing: presales fund about 50% of cost of production (COP); Bhooth Bangla at a illustrative INR100 crore cost had about INR48 crore funded by platforms.
TV and commissioning model: about INR50-55 crore of working capital locked in at any time, as platforms fund production.
Minimum liquidity threshold for motion pictures: INR125-150 crore, per management.
Inventory rose from about INR73 crore to about INR207 crore, mainly Bhooth Bangla, Vvan and Hero Ki Horroin, and is amortised after first monetization.
demand_pricing: Netflix: two new web series in development (a large-scale period drama and another premium show); Lock Upp and Koke (tentative title, February release) on Netflix, plus one Amazon show.
Vertigo TV collaboration for Hindi vertical micro dramas aimed at mobile-first, Gen Z audiences.
TV pricing: management said yields are down 25-30% versus pre-COVID; broadcasters are investing less and owning the IP.
Management says the TV business is shifting toward 6-9 month show tenures, making the production model less lucrative.
Management stated FY27 TV-and-OTT commissioned revenue will offset TV decline, though OTT margins are lower than TV.

qa_highlights.question: What strategic levers are being prioritised in FY27 for OTT and TV, and how are rising production costs managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the commissioned TV, OTT and B2B business rising from about INR160 crore in FY26 to about INR330 crore in FY27, with Netflix and Amazon shows, a Motion Pictures top line near INR400 crore, and new digital verticals.

qa_highlights.question: What capital allocation framework is used to balance digital investment against profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TV and OTT commissioning ties up about INR50-55 crore for around three months, presales cover about 50% of film COP, and the focus has shifted to turnaround time and return on capital.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Bhooth Bangla earn and what is the Q1 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give box-office or share figures on the call, saying the return on capital employed will be visible in Q1 FY27 numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What synergies came from the ALT and Marinating Films amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: ALT's earlier burn of INR125-145 crore a year was cut to about INR6 crore cash loss for digital initiatives; the INR117 crore GST input credit is now a cash asset and no direct tax is expected for 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI being used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an in-house AI team works on short-form reels and shows (award-winning), an AI music library, and planned VFX and production efficiency tools; investment is being scaled cautiously.

qa_highlights.question: Why are TV yields falling and what is the response?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed this to broadcasters playing safe, shorter show tenures and owning the IP; the response is to build owned IP and an OTT B2B pipeline to replace TV volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected business mix in 2-3 years and FY27 revenue visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects motion pictures to exceed 50% of top line and profit within 2-3 years, with TV the smallest contributor, and FY27 revenue near INR800 crore.

risks_watch: FY26 EBITDA and PAT losses persisted; FY27 recovery depends on delivering the INR800 crore plan, of which about INR400 crore relies on motion picture releases.
TV yields are down 25-30% versus pre-COVID, and broadcasters are investing less, which could compress TV margins further.
OTT margins are structurally lower than TV because series are finite, which may dilute profitability as digital revenue grows.
Inventory of about INR207 crore and liquidity of over INR165 crore relative to the INR125-150 crore minimum threshold need monitoring.
Q1 FY27 numbers are the stated checkpoint for the Bhooth Bangla returns and the turnaround.
summary.management_tone: Confident on forward execution and revenue visibility, especially for FY27 and Q1 FY27, but cautious and evasive on specifics: it declined to give Bhooth Bangla box-office or share figures. Management was candid that TV economics are structurally weakening and that OTT margins will be lower than TV.
key_quotes: We have an order book of over INR350 crores plus around INR50 crores gets added each quarter.
So the way we approach now each business is turnaround time and return on capital.

I believe in next 2 to 3 years, this pyramid will shift and Balaji will be more an IP-led content creator with the movie contributing more than 50% to the top line and profitability, followed by digital business.

adds.what: 17-movie pipeline over next 3 years, 4-6 movie releases per year (FY27 has 4 releases)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to ~INR800 crore vs INR210 crore in FY26 (about +280%), led by ~INR400 crore from motion pictures (4 releases, 3 presold), ~INR330 crore TV+OTT+B2B and a ~INR350 crore Netflix order book, though no capacity additions were quantified and FY26 Q4 revenue was not given as a YoY figure.
